10 samples come from the same blog in a 16-day window in July 2026, addressed to the same returning readership with a shared political baseline. The profile cannot show how this voice behaves toward a neutral or hostile audience, in a shorter form, or in a publication requiring formal citation conventions.

Embedded hyperlinks — bare URLs on their own line after most argumentative claims — are a structural feature of this blog's format, not a stylistic choice reproducible in other media. A drafter working in a different medium will need to decide how to handle citations, since this corpus provides no model for prose-embedded footnotes or end-references.

I dropped 5 candidate observations: coined compound epithets (*"word-guessing program," "jobspocalypse"*) — no reproducible counting rule; paragraph-level length variation patterns — counts would have been speculative; a triple-short-sentence opener as a distinct shape — only 1/10 clear instance; trailing qualifications within parentheticals as a distinct function — inseparable from the general parenthetical-span count; and re-use of the piece's title keyword late in the text — only 3/10 samples showed this clearly enough to claim.
